the transient inward Ca2 current (IT) in cat and rat LGN projection cells is activated by depolarization to potentials between ‐65 and ‐55 mV, is blocked by 8 mm‐magnesium or 500 microM nickel ions, and is rapidly inactivated at depolarized membrane potentials.
a transient inward Ca current (I(T)) underlies the low-threshold Ca potentials (LTCs) of cat and rat LGN cells.
a low‐threshold transient Ca2+ current is present in cat and rat thalamic relay neurons and that it is responsible for low‐threshold Ca‐spikes.

the mechanisms of thalamic oscillatory behaviour.
the mechanisms underlying oscillatory behaviour in the central nervous system.
the cellular mechanisms underlying the generation of oscillatory activity in the thalamus.

the low‐threshold calcium potential in the LGN is a T‐type calcium current.

the low‐threshold oscillations of thalamic relay cells are due to an interaction between a T‐type Ca current and a low‐threshold Ca‐dependent K+ current.

the T‐type current is a major contributor to the low‐threshold calcium potentials (LTCs), which are the basis of thalamocortical oscillations in vivo.

the T‐type calcium channel is the main calcium channel in the thalamic relay neurons.
